svg.title: The executor's identity towards Azure DevOps and the rules it meets there
svg.desc: Planned, not built. Left, the cluster: the analyzer and the verifier have no Azure DevOps identity and no token; only the executor has one, through workload identity. Middle, Microsoft Entra ID: a federated credential that trusts the cluster's service account of the executor, and a short-lived access token for Azure DevOps that is short lived, not repo scoped. Right, Azure DevOps: the executor identity is a user of the organization with Basic access and membership of one dedicated group. It may contribute, create branches and contribute to pull requests on the one repository, and a group membership read for reviewer hints is pending an open question and not granted, and it is denied the two bypass-policy permissions, force push, editing policies and managing permissions. The target branch has policies the adapter must find in place before it writes: a minimum number of reviewers with votes reset on new changes and the most recent pusher barred from approving, required reviewers by path who are people, and a required status policy named shadewright/review whose authorized identity is the executor, reset on new changes. People approve and complete the pull request. There is no key in Key Vault and no personal access token.
